title: Projecting Allele Frequency Change under Future Climate Change at Adaptive-Associated Loci
author: Blumstein, Richardson, et al.

steps.title: Run PCA on climate data
steps.instruction: Order the rows of both the past climate Normals file and the future GCM projection file by population so they match, then use prcomp from the vegan package to perform a principal component analysis on the past climate matrix (include all climate variables) with scale=TRUE and center=TRUE. Project the future climate data into the PC space with predict(newdata=…) and inspect the results using biplot from vegan.

substeps.instruction: Order rows in both climate files by population.
Run prcomp on the past climate matrix with scale=TRUE and center=TRUE.
Use predict() with the future climate data as newdata to obtain future PC scores.
Visualize the PCA results with biplot().

steps.title: Fit CCA to allele frequencies
steps.instruction: Merge the past‑climate dataframe and the MAF dataframe by “population name” using base‑R merge, record the column indices for climate and MAF variables, then fit a null canonical correspondence analysis (CCA) with no predictors using cca from vegan with 4,000 permutations. Fit a full CCA including all climate PCs also with 4,000 permutations, and reduce the model by stepwise selection (forward and backward) with ordistep using the null CCA as the starting object and the full model as the scope. Retrieve the final model’s variable significance with $anova.

substeps.instruction: Merge climate and MAF data frames on “population name”.
Record the indices of climate‑PC columns and MAF columns.
Run a null CCA (no predictors) with cca(..., permutations=4000).
Run a full CCA with all climate PCs using cca(..., permutations=4000).
Perform stepwise model selection with ordistep(nullCCA, scope=fullCCA, direction="both").
Use the returned optimal model and call $anova to assess significance of retained predictors.
